clue.text: Where to see Derby County fortunate to miss the beginning

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east

indicators.note: missing its beginning tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for fortunate

parts.note: fortunate means lucky

explanation.surface: A football fan wonders where to watch Derby County, who were lucky to avoid the opening stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby County' looks like the football club, but 'Derby' belongs to the definition and 'County' starts the wordplay. 'to miss the beginning' drops the L of LUCKY, leaving UCKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentucky Derby is a famous American horse race held each year at Churchill Downs in Louisville.

clue.text: Old club portrait

definitions.meaning: the ... Club was an early eighteenth-century Whig literary and political club in London
a portrait of a standard size, less than half-length but showing the hands, named after paintings of that club's members

explanation.definitionFit: The historic Whig club gave its name both to itself and to the size of canvas used for its members' portraits.

clue.text: Bad feeling, but unnecessary to abandon ship

indicators.note: abandoning tells us the letters for ship leave the longer word

parts.note: unnecessary means needless
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor resents being told it was pointless to abandon ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' takes SS out of NEEDLESS. Needle in the sense of hostility is a British informal usage, as in a needle match.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle is informal for antagonism or ill will between rivals, as in a grudge match.

clue.text: Experienced old character going up-river

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: nu is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet
the Derwent is a river in several English counties

explanation.surface: An elderly eccentric is spotted heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns NU into UN. 'old character' suggests an eccentric person, but here it is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undergone something is to have experienced it, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Look — sad piece troubled reflective viewer

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up or disturbed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at a sad bit of writing by a troubled, thoughtful observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' scrambles LOOKSADPIECE. 'reflective viewer' suggests a thoughtful onlooker but describes a toy with mirrors inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a tube with mirrors that reflect coloured fragments into patterns you view through an eyepiece.

clue.text: More work cannot be found anywhere

definitions.text: More work cannot be found anywhere

parts.words: More work cannot be found anywhere
parts.note: Thomas More wrote a book about an ideal state whose Greek-coined name means no place, so his work names somewhere found nowhere

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's book describes an imaginary ideal society whose name means nowhere.

clue.text: Object of Icelandic assembly

definitions.meaning: an object is any physical item or article

explanation.definitionFit: The word means any item, and is also the old Scandinavian term for a governing assembly.

clue.text: I make a mistake in feeble retraction

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word for feeble

parts.note: pale can mean weak or feeble, as in a pale imitation
to nod is to slip up, as in 'even Homer nods'

explanation.surface: Someone admits their error in a weak apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container. Nod meaning to err comes from the saying that even Homer nods, and pale for feeble as in a pale imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A palinode is a poem or statement taking back something said earlier, a formal recantation.

clue.text: Engaged diplomat to daughter

parts.note: an attaché is a junior member of an embassy staff

explanation.surface: A diplomat announces their betrothal to their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged to be married is attached, that is already spoken for.

clue.text: Settle finally at Leeds, perhaps? No, elsewhere in Yorkshire

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged some other way
finally points to the closing letter of the word Settle

explanation.surface: Someone muses about settling down in Leeds, then decides on another part of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E from Settle; 'perhaps' rearranges E with ATLEEDS. Settle and Leeds are both Yorkshire towns, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesdale is a valley region in the north of England, historically part of the North Riding of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Bandage cut

definitions.meaning: a narrow band or strip, such as a headband or binding
a boneless cut of meat or fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a narrow binding strip and a prime boneless piece from a butcher.

clue.text: Butter had to be forfeited to get this yellow wool

definitions.text: Butter had to be forfeited to get this yellow wool

parts.words: Butter had to be forfeited to get this yellow wool
parts.note: a butter is something that butts, a ram; in Greek myth Jason's quest was for the shining coat of a magical ram

explanation.definitionFit: The prize of Jason and the Argonauts was the gilded hide of a winged ram.

clue.text: Ibsen heroine doesn't start getting better

indicators.note: not starting means the surname loses its opening letter

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title character of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An actor playing an Ibsen role has a shaky first night but is improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more able is more capable, hence better at something.

clue.text: Popular and fundamental branch of chemistry

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
organic can mean basic or inherent, part of a thing's structure

explanation.surface: Praise for a well-liked, essential area of science.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry splits into the study of carbon compounds and the study of everything else, which this word labels.

clue.text: Minor part in repeated crime

parts.note: a second go is a repeated one
a fiddle is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: A small-time crook plays a bit part in a repeat offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing this is taking a subordinate role, from the lesser violin part in an orchestra.

clue.text: War diary found at last, ruined in the river

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
at last points to the closing letter of the word found

explanation.surface: A war diary turns up at last, though water-damaged in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives D from found; 'ruined' rearranges WARDIARY with D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irrawaddy is the main river of Myanmar (Burma).

clue.text: Animal set to guard the Cheviots?

definitions.text: Animal set to guard the Cheviots?

parts.words: Animal set to guard the Cheviots?
parts.note: the Cheviot is a breed of sheep, so the animal guarding them is a working dog, though Cheviots also suggests the hills

explanation.definitionFit: A collie or similar working dog is trained to herd and protect a flock.

clue.text: Part of engine performing several functions

definitions.meaning: a pipe with several branches carrying gases to or from an engine's cylinders

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an engine's branched pipework and an adjective for many-sided or diverse.

clue.text: Al's surgery?

parts.note: the letters A and L sit in the very middle of the word health, so a place for Al is the middle of health; a surgery is a doctor's practice

explanation.definitionFit: A local building where doctors and nurses hold clinics is a medical practice or surgery.

clue.text: Rough draft is accurate

definitions.meaning: a memorandum or note of proceedings, a draft record
..., stressed on the second syllable, means precise and detailed

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a brief written record or draft; the adjective means precise in detail.

clue.text: Payment of silver coin to secure books

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone pays a silver coin as a deposit to borrow books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts NT inside REAL. 'books' as the New Testament is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the regular sum paid for the use of property, a hire charge.

clue.text: Terrible places I work in, belonging to the church

indicators.note: in tells us the word for work goes inside the jumbled letters
terrible signals the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A churchman complains about the dreadful places where he works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges PLACESI into EPISCAL, and 'in' puts OP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means governed by bishops, describing churches such as the Anglican one.

clue.text: Mar's disc — an alleged feature of it

definitions.text: Mar's disc — an alleged feature of it

indicators.note: something that features in the words is contained within them, so the letters run across disc and an alleged

explanation.surface: A remark about the face of the red planet and a supposed marking on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is printed Mar's. The letters run from the end of disc through an and into alleged. Astronomers like Lowell once claimed to see long straight channels on Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercourses supposedly seen on Mars by early telescope observers were later shown to be optical illusions.

clue.text: Unblemished, although we absorbed a blow

indicators.note: absorbed means taken inside, so the word for a blow goes within we

parts.note: taken as written
a hit is a blow or strike

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are unmarked even though they took a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' marks the container; 'although' is only a link, giving the surface its concession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unblemished is pure and spotless, qualities the colour symbolises.

clue.text: River in the hills supplies too much water

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for hills

parts.note: downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England

explanation.surface: A river in the hills floods the land around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside DOWNS; the Downs are grassy uplands of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown something is to swamp or flood it, giving it more liquid than it can take.

clue.text: Take in simply fine tune when heard

parts.note: to read is to take in written words
just means simply or merely

explanation.surface: Someone simply absorbs a delicate melody by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine tune when heard' reads as tuning an instrument by ear, the definition stretched to include how it is done; READ and JUST simply run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune something by ear is to make small corrections to it, adjusting it again.

clue.text: Rush about to escape from tormentor

parts.note: to gad is to rush about restlessly, as in gad about
to fly is to flee or escape

explanation.surface: Someone runs around trying to get away from a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a biting insect that pesters livestock, hence any persistent irritating critic.

clue.text: In the pink, I agree

definitions.meaning: in the pink means in good health
a phrase of consent or acceptance, like all right then

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone in fine health and also serves as a reluctant 'all right' of assent.
